official.application_route: Apply for admission to an eligible course (directly via the international application portal or via an authorised agent); the scholarship is assessed automatically with no separate application form.
official.study_mode: Full-time (recipients must maintain a full-time enrolment)
official.citizenship_residency: Must be a citizen of a country other than Australia or New Zealand, be a new international student, and not be a humanitarian or other permanent visa holder; studies must commence at any La Trobe campus in Australia.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship is for international students only, and all applicants are assessed as international applicants under La Trobe's international admission pathway.
official.subject_or_agency_restriction: The program applied for must appear in the published List of eligible courses for 2026 and 2027 (selected undergraduate and postgraduate coursework courses across all campuses).
official.duration: Discount on annual tuition fees for the duration of the course
official.description: La Trobe University states that it values academic excellence and that high-achieving international students considering an undergraduate or postgraduate course will be automatically considered for this scholarship. The scholarship rewards high-achieving international students with up to 25% off annual tuition fees for the duration of studies, with the percentage set by weighted average mark.
official.region: Australia - Melbourne, Bendigo, Albury-Wodonga, Shepparton and Mildura (VIC) and Sydney (NSW) campuses, plus City Campus
official.program_type: Automatic tuition fee discount for high-achieving international students
official.english_requirement: No separate English score is set by the scholarship; applicants must meet the English language entry requirement of their course. Published minimums are IELTS (Academic) overall 6.0 with no band less than 6.0 for undergraduate and overall 6.5 with no band less than 6.0 for postgraduate, with higher scores required for some courses. Equivalent PTE, TOEFL iBT and Cambridge scores are accepted, only the most recent single test achievement is considered, and evidence must be no older than two years unless stated otherwise.

applicant_utility.summary: This is an automatic tuition discount, not a cash scholarship: if your course is on La Trobe's eligible list and your WAM converts to 60-74.9 you are looking at 20% off annual tuition fees, and 75 or above lifts you to 25%. Nothing extra is submitted - the outcome is written into your Letter of Offer, so the real work is making sure your admission application, WAM evidence and English results are all in order before you apply. Because the discount applies only to tuition, you must independently fund accommodation, Overseas Student Health Cover, flights and daily living costs, so budget for those out of pocket. If you apply to the Sydney campus, note that the discount only starts in your second semester, so the first semester must be funded at full fee.
applicant_utility.best_fit: New international students with an Australian-equivalent WAM of 60 or above, no sponsorship, applying for an eligible undergraduate or postgraduate coursework course at a Victorian La Trobe campus.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your exact course title against the published eligible-course list for 2026 and 2027 before you apply, since a course missing from that list will not be assessed
Work out how your overseas qualification converts to a WAM or ATAR band, because the 20% versus 25% tier is decided by that mark alone
Hold an IELTS Academic (or accepted equivalent) result less than two years old that meets your course's minimum, since expired evidence is a common blocker
Get academic documents certified by an approved certifier before uploading, and include certified translations for any non-English originals
Prepare Genuine Student evidence of genuine access to funds, because the scholarship cannot be considered until the Genuine Student assessment including financial checks is passed
Diarise the reduced acceptance deposit deadline in your Letter of Offer, since failing to pay it on time can cause the scholarship to be withdrawn
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a course that is not on the eligible list - the scholarship simply will not be assessed, and the list is refreshed each year
Being classified as sponsored: a full fee-paying, non-sponsored status is mandatory, so any employer, government or family sponsor funding your fees disqualifies you
Holding humanitarian or permanent visa status, or being an Australian or New Zealand citizen, which removes eligibility entirely
Failing the Genuine Student assessment including financial checks before consideration, often due to thin or unexplained funds evidence
Missing the acceptance deposit due date in the Letter of Offer, which can cause the scholarship to be withdrawn even after it has been awarded
Deferring the intake or not securing a student visa for that intake, both of which put the offer at risk of revocation
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs, accommodation, Overseas Student Health Cover, flights and visa costs, textbooks and course equipment, and any graduation or official document fees are all outside the award; the university states that scholarships on its international scholarships pages apply to tuition fees only and do not cover living costs, accommodation or other expenses.
document_audit: Every copied document must be certified by an accepted certifier such as an Australian overseas diplomatic mission, public notary, La Trobe authorised agent or the issuing institution, and scanned in full colour and clearly labelled
A translated document needs a certified copy of the original alongside the certified translation, not just the translated version
Where more than one English test has been taken, only the most recent single achievement counts for admission
Academic documents must be certified before offer acceptance can be finalised, not after arrival
Applicants under 18 at commencement must add Form 157N and a signed offer acceptance form from a parent or approved guardian
alerts: Sydney campus applicants get the discount from the second semester only, so first-semester tuition must be financed at the full rate
The scholarship may not be deferred to future intakes or years, and the offer may be revoked if a student visa for that intake cannot be secured
There is no separate scholarship form, so there is no way to 'apply well' for this award - the deciding factor is your academic mark plus course eligibility

The award can be combined with the Early Acceptance Grant for a larger first-year discount, but every condition of both offers must be met, so check whether an early acceptance deadline applies to your offer

Consider this alongside larger La Trobe international awards such as the Vice Chancellor Scholarship (up to 100%) which do require a separate application and a written statement if your WAM is 80 or above
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit one admission application for an eligible course through La Trobe's international application portal or an authorised agent, meet the Genuine Student assessment, then accept the Letter of Offer and pay the reduced deposit by its due date - the scholarship percentage appears in that offer.
